decisions.question: SDD pre-flight for nidana.model.3, a gate-only phase whose plan carries complete code verified by a dry run against the real replay tool: which model implements the tasks?

options.label: Sonnet for every task
options.consequence: Transcription plus the replay, at a mid-tier cost; reviews still catch drift from the plan.

options.label: Opus for the declaration tasks
options.consequence: More cost for transcription the plan's dry run already settled.

decisions.why: S97 put opus on full-review implementers only; SDD's model rule gives transcription of complete plan code the cheapest workable tier, and the run keeps mid-tier as the floor for prose-heavy dartdoc.

decisions.question: The run rules told every implementer to end its commits with a Claude Opus 5.5 co-author trailer whatever model it runs on; a sonnet implementer followed its own harness's attribution (Claude Sonnet 5.5) instead, which is the accurate one. Which trailer do subagent commits carry from here on?

options.label: The model that wrote the commit, as the subagent's harness attribution names it
options.consequence: Attribution in git history is accurate from here on; earlier sonnet-written commits keep the Opus trailer, which the report lists.

options.label: Keep the uniform Opus trailer
options.consequence: Uniform history that misattributes every sonnet-written commit.

decisions.chosen: The model that wrote the commit, as the subagent's harness attribution names it
decisions.why: A co-author trailer is a statement of who wrote the change; uniformity is no reason to misstate it. The run never amends commits, so earlier ones stay as written and the report says which tasks sonnet implemented.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md, Notes for the report (trailer note)

decisions.question: Which Learnings does nidana.model.3's slim verification doc carry, with which proposed dispositions?

options.label: Four, each dropped with a reason: the Interface's angle-bracket renderings, the lockfile wording, nidana.model.6's loose Verification sentence, the size against the estimate
options.consequence: Every gate-time finding about the tree is visible at sign-off; the doc-comment one names the end-of-node contract touch that can absorb it.

options.label: Only the doc-comment finding
options.consequence: Shorter, but the owner would not see that the phase plan's lockfile wording and nidana.model.6's Verification sentence are loose.

decisions.chosen: Four, each dropped with a reason: the Interface's angle-bracket renderings, the lockfile wording, nidana.model.6's loose Verification sentence, the size against the estimate
decisions.why: The template asks for every gate-time finding about the tree; none of the four changes a result today. The run will batch compatible contract touches found during the node into one governance sweep after nidana.model.14 rather than interrupt each phase for a doc-comment edit.

decisions.question: nidana.model.3's final review reads 'ready to merge: yes' with minor findings only (the purity test's directive reader misses conditional and raw-string imports; D6's token list has gaps; the README overstates; dropped trailing comments). Run a fix wave, or route them?

options.label: Merge without a fix wave; route each finding to the phase that next edits the code (nidana.model.4 for the purity test, nidana.model.8 for comments and the README) or to the end-of-node governance sweep (D6)
options.consequence: The phase merges as reviewed; each finding lands where its code changes next, and the routed list carries it across context summaries.

options.label: A fix wave now
options.consequence: Fixes land sooner, at the cost of another implementer and re-review for findings the reviewer triaged as can-wait.

decisions.chosen: Merge without a fix wave; route each finding to the phase that next edits the code (nidana.model.4 for the purity test, nidana.model.8 for comments and the README) or to the end-of-node governance sweep (D6)
decisions.why: SDD's fix wave answers final-review findings that must be fixed before the merge; the reviewer triaged every one as can-wait. The purity test hardening should land before nidana.model.4 adds libraries, so it is routed there rather than dropped.

notes: SDD controller rulings are the decisions here; the per-task review log is docs/auto-run/steps/S107.sdd-progress.md.
Dispatches: 4 implementers (sonnet), 4 task reviews (sonnet), 1 final review (opus); no fix round.
